claim: The World Economic Forum's 'Meat: the Future' white-paper series, beginning with 'Alternative Proteins' (January 2019), positions plant-based products, cultured/lab-grown meat, and insects as substitutes for conventional animal protein, framing the shift as a pathway to lower greenhouse-gas emissions and feed a projected 10-billion population. A companion WEF analysis stated that balancing diets with alternative proteins could cut diet-related deaths by about 5% and food-related emissions by about 25%.

sources.label: World Economic Forum — White Paper, 'Meat: the Future series — Alternative Proteins' (January 2019)
sources.quote: Alternative proteins that can act as substitutes for traditional animal-based food are attracting considerable financial investment, research attention and interest in the media as a pathway to meeting the nutritional needs and food demands of a predicted mid-century population of 10 billion, in a healthy and sustainable manner.

notes: The WEF white paper and press release are public and explicitly advocate scaling alternative proteins (plant-based, cultured, insect) as substitutes for conventional animal protein on climate/health grounds — the reel's 'open published fact' framing is accurate as to the documents' existence and content. The reel's gloss 'declared a war on traditional meat consumption' is editorial; the papers frame it as one of three pathways to sustainable protein, not a ban. This record asserts only what the documents say; it does not assert the reel's further inference that this advocacy is connected to tick-borne meat allergy (see 2023-alpha-gal-001, 2021-oxitec-gates-tick-001).
